# 3 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Ptolemy Struck Down and Then Persecutes

---

**1** He had scarcely finished this prayer when the high priest Shimon, struck with awe and trembling, addressed Ptolemy: O Ptolemy, this great God who looks down from on high and watches over all things did not consecrate this place for the sake of the wicked or for those who seek to enter it in violation of the law.

**2** He struck down the former Heliodorus, who came with a full army to plunder the treasury, and drove him away in disgrace.

**3** And now too, seeing you as one who has acted against the laws, he will not fail to punish you.

**4** He had barely finished speaking when Ptolemy was seized with a great terror, and he was struck in all his limbs and drained of all his strength.

**5** His companions saw him fall down and in haste carried him out, seized as he was with such great dread.

**6** So when God had exercised his judgment in this way, Ptolemy was no longer able to carry out any of his threats.

**7** He returned to Egypt, filled with bitterness of heart; but God had delivered the people from peril.

**8** When Ptolemy had returned to Egypt, however, and had grown worse in his wickedness, aided by the worthless drinking companions he had around him who were strangers to justice, he was not content with his earlier wicked deeds.

**9** He uttered threats against the Jews, and had a letter composed commanding his soldiers to seize all the Jews and imprison them wherever any of them might be found.

**10** When the letter was sent out, it read: King Ptolemy Philopator to the generals and soldiers in Egypt and all its territories, greetings.

**11** I am well, as are my affairs.

**12** Since our campaign into Asia has gone as we intended, and we have returned safely, we have resolved, not by the use of force but through benevolence and great generosity, to extend our beneficence to the inhabitants of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

**13** As for the Jews in those regions, they received us warmly and greeted us enthusiastically, and they accompanied us to where we went and showed themselves favorable to us in all respects.

**14** However, many of these same Jews are found to be troublemakers who do not submit to our rule, and they treat our sacred precincts with contempt.

**15** Therefore, being motivated by kindness rather than severity, we have decided that they be registered among us.

**16** They are to be enrolled in a census, assigned to the grade of those who serve in our household, and all those registered are to be branded with the ivy-leaf emblem of Dionysus and reduced to the inferior status of before.

**17** Those who choose not to accept this reduced standing shall be arrested and disciplined; those who resist with contempt shall be executed.

**18** Our aim in all of this is to place them on an equal standing with ourselves and to bring them to abandon their foreign and barbaric customs.

**19** Anyone who betrays a Jew or delivers him into our hands shall receive the confiscated property of the one betrayed as a reward.

**20** When this decree was read out in Egypt, it produced great sorrow throughout the land.

**21** The Jews mourned deeply and wept with great bitterness of heart.

**22** Everywhere there was lamentation, and weeping and grief filled the streets.

**23** Those of gentle spirit wept even for those who were in a lower condition than themselves.

**24** Grief filled every household, and sighing and lamentation did not cease.

**25** All Egypt was filled with mourning, and no one was untouched by the plight of the Jews.
